1.word_for_word: ṣaṭ-catvāriṃśake — in the forty-sixth chapter; ghoṣam uddhavam preṣya — sending Uddhava to the cowherd settlement; tad-girā — through Uddhava's words; yaśodā-nandayoḥ śoka-apanodanam — removing the grief of Yaśodā and Nanda; kāma-cāram parityajya — abandoning unrestricted conduct; ati-saṃyataḥ — thoroughly disciplined; guroḥ jñānam anujñāpya — receiving his teacher's permission after learning; sakhyā uddhavena gopīḥ upādiśat — he instructed the gopīs through his friend Uddhava; gopīnām sāntvanam ati-rahasyam — consoling the gopīs is exceedingly confidential; san-mantri-sādhyam — a task requiring a trustworthy counselor; vṛṣṇīnām buddhi-sattamaḥ — the finest intellect among the Vṛṣṇis
1.translation: In the forty-sixth chapter Kṛṣṇa sends Uddhava to the cowherd settlement and, through Uddhava's words, removes the grief of Yaśodā and Nanda. Having lived as a disciplined twice-born student, renounced unrestricted conduct and completed his studies with his teacher's permission, Kṛṣṇa now entrusts his friend with the gopīs. Their consolation is an extremely confidential matter, one that requires a wise and trustworthy counselor; hence Uddhava is described as the finest intellect among the Vṛṣṇis.

4.word_for_word: gopīnām viśeṣataḥ sandeśe kāraṇam — the reason for a special message to the gopīs; mayi eva saṅkalpa-ātmakam manaḥ yāsām — whose resolving mind is fixed in me alone; aham eva prāṇaḥ yāsām — for whom I alone am life itself; mad-arthe tyaktāḥ daihikāḥ pati-putra-ādayaḥ yābhiḥ — who gave up bodily relations such as husband and children for my sake; man-nimittam tyaktau loka-dharmau — who abandoned worldly and religious conventions on my account; iha-amutra-sukhe tat-sādhanāni ca — pleasures in this world and the next and the means to them; tān bibharmi — I sustain them; poṣayāmi saṃvardhayāmi sukhayāmi — nourish, protect, increase and make them happy
4.translation: Kṛṣṇa explains why the gopīs require a special message. Their very faculty of resolve is fixed on him alone; he alone is their life. For his sake they relinquished bodily relationships such as husband and children, and for him they gave up conventional worldly and religious pursuits, together with the pleasures promised in this world and the next and the means of attaining them. ‘I maintain such people’ means: I sustain, nourish, protect, cause them to flourish and bring them happiness.

5.word_for_word: tāsām viyoga-ādhim darśayati dvayena — two verses show the affliction of their separation; viraheṇa yat autkaṇṭhyam — the intense longing caused by separation; tena vihvalāḥ — overwhelmed and helpless through it
5.translation: The next two verses describe the gopīs' affliction in separation. Their longing born from separation has made them overwhelmed and helpless.

6.word_for_word: gokulāt nirgamanasamaye — when departing from Gokula; śīghram āgamiṣyāmi iti — ‘I shall return soon’; pratyāgamana-sandeśāḥ — messages promising return; me madīyāḥ vallavyaḥ — my own cowherd women; mad-ātmikāḥ — whose self is in me; tāsām ātmā sva-dehe yadi syāt — if their self still remained in their own body; viraha-tāpena dahyeta eva — it would surely be burned by separation; mayi vartamānatvāt — because their self exists in me; kathañcit jīvanti — they somehow remain alive
6.translation: When Kṛṣṇa left Gokula he sent promises that he would return soon. Those promises keep the gopīs alive. They are ‘mine’ in the deepest sense: their very selves are established in me. If their consciousness still remained centered in their own bodies, the fire of separation would have consumed them; they live somehow only because their being is centered in Kṛṣṇa.

7.word_for_word: sandeśam — the message; bhavatīnām viyogaḥ me na hi sarvātmanā kvacit — ‘your separation from me is never absolute in any respect’; ity-ādikam — and similar teachings
7.translation: The message Uddhava carries begins with the assurance that the gopīs are never in any absolute sense separated from Kṛṣṇa and continues with teachings of that kind.

8.word_for_word: nimlocati — as the sun was setting; astam gacchati sati — when it went to the horizon; channam yānam yasya — whose vehicle was concealed; gopībhiḥ ajñātatvena — without the gopīs noticing him; nanda-saṅgam labdhavān — he obtained a private meeting with Nanda
8.translation: Uddhava arrived as the sun was setting. The statement that his vehicle was concealed suggests that the gopīs did not notice his arrival, allowing him first to obtain a private meeting with Nanda.

9.word_for_word: vrajam varṇayati pañcabhiḥ — five verses describe Vraja; vāsitāḥ — cows in heat; puṣpavatyaḥ gāvaḥ — fertile cows; tat-nimittam abhitaḥ yudhyadbhiḥ — bulls fighting around them on that account; śuṣmibhiḥ mattaiḥ vṛṣaiḥ — powerful excited bulls; nāditam — resounding; vāsrābhiḥ dhenubhiḥ — by lowing cows; sva-vatsakān prati — calling to their calves
9.translation: Five verses describe the evening scene in Vraja. Fertile cows were in heat, and powerful excited bulls fought around them. The settlement resounded with the lowing of cows calling to their calves.

10.word_for_word: vilaṅghadbhiḥ utpatadbhiḥ — with animals leaping and springing; go-doha-śabdaiḥ saha — together with sounds of milking; muñca mā muñca naya ānaya dehi gṛhāṇa ity-ādayaḥ — cries such as ‘release,’ ‘do not release,’ ‘take,’ ‘bring,’ ‘give,’ ‘hold’; veṇūnām niḥsvanena maṇḍitam — adorned with the sound of flutes
10.translation: Animals leapt about while the noise of milking filled the settlement, together with the ordinary cries of the workers—‘let her go,’ ‘don't let her go,’ ‘take this,’ ‘bring that,’ ‘give it,’ ‘hold it.’ The sound of flutes ornamented the whole scene.

11.word_for_word: gāyantībhiḥ gopībhiḥ — by singing gopīs; gopaiḥ ca — and by cowherd men; su-virājitam — made splendid
11.translation: Vraja appeared especially beautiful with the gopīs and cowherd men singing.

12.word_for_word: agni-ādi-arcanā-anvitaiḥ gopa-gṛhaiḥ — cowherd homes engaged in worship of fire and the other deities; dhūpa-ādibhiḥ manoramam — charming with incense and other offerings
12.translation: The cowherd homes were engaged in their evening worship of fire and the other deities, and incense and other offerings made the settlement delightful.

13.word_for_word: ṣaṇḍaḥ — a group; samūhaḥ — a cluster

14.word_for_word: ārcayat — worshiped, honored; pūjayām āsa — received with ceremonial respect
14.translation: Nanda ‘ārcayat’ Uddhava—he worshiped and honored him as a guest.

15.word_for_word: kaśipau — on a couch or bed; śayyāyām — upon the bed; saṃviṣṭam — seated or reclining
15.translation: Uddhava was comfortably seated or reclined upon a couch.

17.word_for_word: diṣṭyā iti — in the expression with diṣṭyā; karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī — a genitive used with the object; hiṃsā-arthānām prayoge — a grammatical usage found with verbs conveying injury
17.translation: Śrīdhara notes the grammatical construction: the genitive associated with ‘diṣṭyā’ is used in the object relation, as also occurs with certain verbs expressing harm.

18.word_for_word: gāvaḥ — cows; girim — the mountain; govardhanam — Govardhana
18.translation: The ‘mountain’ referred to is Govardhana, and ‘go’ refers to the cows.

19.word_for_word: api āyāsyati — will he perhaps come?; āgamiṣyati kim — will he return?
19.translation: Nanda's question is simply: ‘Will he perhaps come back? Will Kṛṣṇa return?’

20.word_for_word: śrī-kṛṣṇa-upakāra-smaraṇa-ādibhiḥ — by remembering Kṛṣṇa's favors and protection; anupama-ānandena abhibhūyamānaḥ — overwhelmed by incomparable joy; dāvāgneḥ — from the forest fire; vātāt varṣāt ca — from wind and rain; vṛṣāt sarpāt ca — from the bull and serpent; anyebhyaḥ duratikramebhyaḥ mṛtyubhyaḥ — from other unavoidable mortal dangers; śrī-kṛṣṇena rakṣitāḥ smaḥ — we were protected by Kṛṣṇa
20.translation: As Nanda remembers Kṛṣṇa's many acts of protection, incomparable joy overwhelms him. ‘We were saved by Śrī Kṛṣṇa from the forest fire, from wind and torrential rain, from the demonic bull and serpent, and from many other deadly dangers that no ordinary person could have overcome.’

21.word_for_word: smaratām — for those remembering him; līlayā apāṅgena nirīkṣitam — the playful sidelong glance he cast; aṅga he uddhava — dear Uddhava
21.translation: Nanda remembers in particular Kṛṣṇa's playful sidelong glances. ‘Aṅga’ is an affectionate address: ‘Dear Uddhava.’

22.word_for_word: na kevalam śithilāḥ eva — their attachments do not merely become loosened; śanaiḥ uparamanti — gradually they cease altogether; saritaḥ ca vana-uddeśāḥ ca — rivers and regions of forest; tān ākrīḍān — those playgrounds; krīḍā-sthānāni — places of Kṛṣṇa's play
22.translation: By remembering Kṛṣṇa, worldly bonds are not merely loosened; they gradually cease. Nanda's mind turns instead to the rivers and forest regions that served as the places of Kṛṣṇa's play.

23.word_for_word: surāṇām arthāya — for the sake of the gods; mahat gambhīram — weighty and profound; gargasyā vacanam yathā — like the statement of Garga
23.translation: Nanda recalls Garga's weighty and profound words, spoken in connection with the welfare of the gods.

24.word_for_word: na kevalam tad-vacaḥ-anusāreṇa eva — not only in accordance with Garga's words; vyavahāra-saṃvādāt api — but also because events themselves correspond to them; kaṃsam iti — this is expressed in the statement beginning with Kaṃsa
24.translation: The conclusion that Kṛṣṇa is extraordinary rests not only on Garga's prophecy; actual events have repeatedly corresponded to that prophecy, beginning with what has happened to Kaṃsa.

25.word_for_word: ibha-rāṭ — king of elephants; yaṣṭim iva — like a stick; tāla-traya-pramāṇam dhanuḥ — the bow measuring three tālas; babhañja — broke
25.translation: Kṛṣṇa broke the enormous bow, three tālas in measure, as easily as a lordly elephant might snap a stick.

31.word_for_word: akhila-gurutvam — being teacher and source of all; janakatvena niyantṛtvena ca — as progenitor and controller; rāmaḥ mukundaḥ ca — Rāma and Mukunda; viśvasya bīja-yonī — seed and womb of the universe; nimitta-upādāne — efficient and material causes; puruṣaḥ aṃśaḥ — Puruṣa is their portion; pradhānam śaktiḥ — Pradhāna is their power; pradhāna-puruṣau api etau eva — these two themselves are Pradhāna and Puruṣa in ultimate dependence; bhūteṣu anupraviśya — entering into the beings; bhūtānām jñānasya jīvasya ca īśāte — they rule both consciousness conditioned by beings and the jīvas; purāṇau anādī — ancient, beginningless; anāditvāt kāraṇatvam — because beginningless, they are causal; tataḥ niyantṛtvam — hence they are controllers
31.translation: Uddhava establishes their universal supremacy as both source and controller. Rāma and Mukunda are the ‘seed and womb’ of the universe—that is, its efficient and material causes. Although Puruṣa and Pradhāna are ordinarily identified as those causes, the Puruṣa is their manifestation and Pradhāna their power; ultimately those two causes depend upon Rāma and Kṛṣṇa themselves. Entering every being, they govern the individual jīva and the conditioned forms of consciousness associated with embodied existence. They are beginningless; from being beginningless follows their causal status, and from causal status their governing sovereignty.

32.word_for_word: sṛṣṭi-ādi-karma-āveśāt manuṣya-ādi-janma-darśanāt ca — because he appears involved in creation and takes human and other births; tasya anyebhyaḥ kaḥ viśeṣaḥ — what distinguishes him from ordinary beings?; karma-āśayam karma-vāsanām nirhṛtya — removing the deposit and latent tendency of karma; brahma-mayaḥ — absorbed in Brahman; svarūpa-jñānavān — possessing realization of true nature; arka-varṇaḥ — radiant like the sun; śuddha-sattva-mūrtiḥ — of pure-sattva form; parām gatim tat padam yāti — attains the supreme destination, his state
32.translation: An objection may arise: if Kṛṣṇa appears to engage in cosmic activity and even takes human birth, how does he differ from ordinary embodied beings? The verse answers by describing the result of knowing him. One who casts off the latent store of karma, becomes established in Brahman and realizes the true Self, radiant like the sun in a form of pure sattva, attains the supreme destination—his state. This could not be so if Kṛṣṇa were merely another conditioned being.

33.word_for_word: akhilasya ātmā ca hetuḥ ca — Self and cause of all; tasmin kāraṇena manuṣya-ākṛtau — in that cause appearing in human form; mahātmani paripūrṇe — in the complete Great Self; bhavantau bhaktim kurutaḥ — you two direct your devotion; kṛta-kṛtyau — therefore you have accomplished what is to be accomplished
33.translation: He is both the Self and the cause of everything, yet that complete Great Self now appears in human form. Because Nanda and Yaśodā have directed their devotion toward him in precisely that form, their purpose in life is already fully accomplished.

34.word_for_word: prastutam āha — he returns to the immediate subject; āgamiṣyati iti — ‘he will come’; pitroḥ yuvayoḥ — to you two, his parents
34.translation: Uddhava returns to the immediate point: Kṛṣṇa will come back to the two of you, his parents.

35.word_for_word: yāta yūyam vrajam tāta — ‘Father, you go to Vraja’; vayam ca snehaduḥkhitān jñātīn vaḥ draṣṭum eṣyāmaḥ — ‘we shall come to see our relatives who suffer in love’; vidhāya suhṛdām sukham — after bringing happiness to our friends; tat satyam kariṣyati — Kṛṣṇa will make that promise true
35.translation: Kṛṣṇa himself had promised: ‘Father, you return to Vraja. After arranging the welfare of our friends here, we will come to see all of you, our relatives who suffer from love for us.’ Uddhava assures them that Kṛṣṇa will make that promise true.

36.word_for_word: kāla-vilambanam asahamānau — unable to tolerate even the delay in time; mā khidyatam — do not grieve; he mahābhāgau — O greatly fortunate pair; antike — near, close by; idānīm eva samīpe — even now close to you; antar-hṛdi — within the heart; jyotiḥ iva edhasi — like fire within wood; mathanam vinā na dṛśyate — it is not seen without friction; bhaktim vinā kṛṣṇaḥ api na dṛśyate — similarly Kṛṣṇa is not seen without devotion
36.translation: Because Nanda and Yaśodā cannot bear even the delay until Kṛṣṇa's physical return, Uddhava tells them, ‘Do not grieve, greatly fortunate ones; he is near you even now, within the heart.’ Why is he not visible to everyone? Like fire latent within wood, which is not manifested without friction, Kṛṣṇa is not perceived without devotion.

37-39.word_for_word: ati-priyān pitṛ-ādīn vihāya iha āgamanam na saṅgacchate iti manyeta — one might think his coming here is incompatible with leaving his dearest parents; asya priya-ādayaḥ na hi santi — ultimately he has no intrinsically beloved and nonbeloved; amāninaḥ — free from egoic self-estimation; samānasya — equal toward all; janma-karma-ādi-rahitaḥ api — though free from conditioned birth and action; krīḍā-prayojanaḥ san — acting for the sake of līlā; sādhūnām paripālanāya — for protection of the good; sat-asat-miśra-yoniṣu — in sattvic, rajasic and tamasic births, or mixed species; deva-matsya-nṛsiṃha-ādi-yoniṣu — as gods, fish, Narasiṃha and other forms; kalpate — manifests
37-39.translation: One might think that Kṛṣṇa's coming to Mathurā cannot be reconciled with abandoning his most beloved parents and friends. Uddhava answers that in the ultimate sense he has no one who is intrinsically ‘beloved’ or ‘unbeloved’: he is free from egoic partiality and equal toward all. Although untouched by conditioned birth and action, he nevertheless manifests for the purpose of līlā and for protecting the good, appearing in sattvic, rajasic, tamasic and mixed orders of birth—or, under another interpretation, in divine, aquatic, Narasiṃha and many other forms.

40.word_for_word: janma-karma-ādi-rahitasya kutaḥ etat — how can one free of birth and action engage in such manifestations?; krīḍām atītaḥ api krīḍan — though beyond play in the conditioned sense, he plays; māyā-guṇaiḥ ghaṭate — it is made possible through the guṇas of māyā
40.translation: How can one who is in truth beyond birth and karmic action nevertheless appear to perform such deeds? Though transcending conditioned activity, he plays through the guṇas of his māyā; this explains the appearance without compromising his transcendence.

41.word_for_word: avidyā-upādheḥ jīvasya kartṛtvam dṛṣṭāntī-kurvan — using the jīva's apparent agency under ignorance as an analogy; bhramarikā paribhramaṇam — spinning around; tayā upalakṣitayā dṛṣṭyā — through vision affected by that spinning; bhūḥ api bhrāmyati iti pratīyate — the earth appears to spin; citte kartari sati — although the mind is the actual operative factor; tatra citte aham-dhiyā ātma-adhyāsena — through superimposing the self upon mind by the ‘I’ notion; ātmā kartā smṛtaḥ — the Self is imagined to be the doer
41.translation: Śrīdhara illustrates apparent agency through the conditioned jīva. When a person spins around, his affected vision makes the stationary earth appear to spin. Likewise, although the mind is the operative factor in conditioned action, the ‘I’ notion superimposes the Self upon that mind and one therefore imagines, ‘I, the Self, am the doer.’ Kṛṣṇa's apparent involvement in māyic activity should be understood as no more binding than this—indeed less so, because his māyā is under his control.

42.word_for_word: yuvayoḥ eva na ayam ātmajaḥ — he is not your son alone; sarveṣām api — he belongs to all; na ātmajaḥ eva — not merely a son; śatru-mitra-ādi-rūpaḥ api — he also appears in relations such as enemy and friend; sarva-ātmatva-nirūpaṇena — by establishing that he is the Self of all; moha-nivṛttaye — in order to remove delusion; sambandham anaikāntikī-karoti — Uddhava relativizes exclusive bodily relationship
42.translation: Kṛṣṇa is not exclusively the son of Nanda and Yaśodā, nor is ‘son’ his only relationship. He may stand in every relation—friend, enemy and so on—because he is the Self of all. By explaining this universal identity, Uddhava loosens their insistence on an exclusive bodily relationship and seeks to relieve the delusion born from separation.

43.word_for_word: acyutāt vinā — apart from Acyuta; tarām nitarām — absolutely, in the fullest sense; tattvataḥ vācyam nirvacana-arham vastu na asti — no entity exists that can truly be defined as separate
43.translation: Apart from Acyuta there is, in the fullest ontological sense, no independently definable reality at all.

44.word_for_word: dīpān nirūpya prajvālya — arranging and lighting lamps; vāstūn — house-parts; dehalī-ādīn — thresholds and similar places
44.translation: They arranged and lit the lamps and attended to the household places such as thresholds and entrances.

45.word_for_word: maṇibhiḥ kāñcī-ādiṣu sthitaiḥ — with jewels set in girdles and other ornaments; rajjūḥ vikarṣatsu bhujeṣu kaṅkaṇānām srajaḥ yāsām — whose armlets and bracelets formed rows on arms pulling the ropes; calantaḥ nitambāḥ stanāḥ hārāḥ ca — hips, breasts and necklaces moving; kuṇḍalaiḥ tviṣantaḥ sphurantaḥ kapolāḥ — cheeks flashing with earrings; aruṇāni kuṅkumāni yeṣu ānanāni — faces reddened with kuṅkuma
45.translation: As the women worked, jewels shone from their girdles and other ornaments; bracelets formed shining rows along the arms that pulled the ropes. Their hips, breasts and necklaces moved with the effort, earrings flashed against their cheeks, and kuṅkuma gave a reddish glow to their faces.

47.word_for_word: tadā vraja-okasaḥ gopyaḥ — at that time, the gopīs residing in Vraja
47.translation: The women referred to here are the gopīs dwelling in Vraja.

48.word_for_word: sa-krodham āhuḥ — they speak angrily; akrūra iti — ‘Akrūra’; artham sādhitavān — he accomplished the assigned purpose; artha-sādhakaḥ — one who successfully carries out a task; yena nītaḥ iti — ‘by whom Kṛṣṇa was taken away’
48.translation: The gopīs speak with anger about Akrūra. He was indeed an ‘artha-sādhaka,’ one who successfully accomplished the mission entrusted to him—namely, the one by whom Kṛṣṇa was taken away from them.

49.word_for_word: kaṃsam ghātayitvā punaḥ kim-artham āgataḥ — after having Kaṃsa killed, why has he come again?; svayam eva kāraṇam sambhāvayanti — the gopīs themselves speculate about the reason; tadā sādhitena kāryeṇa prītasya bhartuḥ — perhaps his master was pleased by the task accomplished; pāṭhāntare pretasya mṛtasya kaṃsasya niṣkṛtim aurdhva-dehikam — under another reading, funeral recompense for the dead Kaṃsa; asmābhiḥ kṛtvā sādhayiṣyate kim — will he use us to perform it?; asmat-māṃsaiḥ piṇḍān kṛtvā dāsyati — will he make funeral balls from our flesh?; kṛtāhnikaḥ uddhavaḥ āgataḥ — while they spoke thus, Uddhava arrived after completing his morning rites
49.translation: They wonder angrily why Akrūra would have returned after accomplishing the task of bringing Kṛṣṇa and thereby causing Kaṃsa's death. Perhaps, they speculate, his master was pleased with his successful mission and has sent him again. Under another textual reading, they make a darker joke: ‘Has he come to perform the dead Kaṃsa's funeral rites by using us—will he make the funeral offerings from our own flesh?’ While the women were speaking in this way, Uddhava approached after completing his morning ablutions and prescribed rites.
